topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture framework, learning outcomes, and foundational concepts regarding the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Growth signaling pathways and sustained proliferation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream signaling cascades dysregulate proliferation and survival pathways.

topics.label: Differentiation block in hematopoietic and epithelial cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how impaired cellular differentiation contributes to cancer development in both leukemias and solid tumors.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through p53 pathway inactivation and Bcl-2 family dysregulation.

topics.label: Telomeres, replicative senescence, and genome protection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address telomere dynamics, cellular senescence, and p53-mediated stress responses that regulate replicative immortality.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the metabolic adaptations of cancer cells, including aerobic glycolysis, global metabolic rewiring, and oncometabolite production.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the mechanisms and triggers by which developing tumors induce new blood vessel growth to sustain oxygen and nutrient delivery.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genetics of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the sequential biological steps, monitoring methods, environmental factors, and genomic features associated with cancer metastasis.

topics.label: Summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: It provides closing remarks summarizing how hallmarks integrate across tumor development and wraps up the lecture.
